newsitem.title: CANADA: Canfor seen in lead for TimberWest.
newsitem.headline: Canfor seen in lead for TimberWest.

text.p: A deal for the sale of TimberWest Forest Ltd is likely to be announced before Christmas and analysts speculated Friday that Canfor Corp would emerge the winner.

TimberWest said in October it and 52-percent shareholder Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd agreed to offer the lumber producer for sale. Bids were submitted last week and Stephen Bellringer, a TimberWest director overseeing the sale process, said Friday the firm aims for a deal by Christmas. "Discussions are ongoing," he said, declining further comment.

Analysts said Vancouver-based Canfor was seen as the leading contender. It is short of timber and was thwarted in an effort last year to acquire Slocan Forest Products Ltd. A Canfor spokesman declined comment.
"Canfor seems like the only logical one given its fiber-deficit situation. That's who is being talked about," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
TimberWest shares rose 0.30 to 19.80. An article in the Financial Post also focused on Canfor as the likely winner.
Analysts said speculation centered on a winning bid of at least C$21 a share or C$643 million in total.

But the price could be as high as C$27 a share depending on the maturity of TimberWest's forest base, they said. "C$27 is the number you come up with based on previous transactions, the sale of private timberland in Canada and sales in the U.S.," said one analyst.

Analyst John Duncanson of Duncanson Investment Research said he saw Canfor as the most likely buyer but did not expect it to pay more than C$23 a share. He also held out the possibility that Canfor could buy Fletcher's 52 percent stake and not acquire the remaining shares. "It's a good fit. Canfor basically wants the coastal timber," he said.

TimberWest has five lumber mills with a total annual capacity of 685 million board feet and owns 210,000 hectares of private timberlands which along with its government timber tenures provide an annual harvest of 4.2 million cubic meters of wood.
Deacon Capital analyst Brian Topp said he felt TimberWest was "fully valued" around C$20 to C$21 a share. Many buyers "would struggle to make money upwards of 21 or even at 21," he said.

The sale is subject to provincial government approval but analysts did not anticipate it to block a sale to Canfor because the deal would not lead to a significant concentration of forest assets in its hands in any region of the province.
